name: Visual Genome
description: Visual Genome is a dataset designed to enable comprehensive scene understanding by connecting language and vision. It contains 108,249 images densely annotated with region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. Each image has an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, 18 relationships, and 42 region descriptions. The dataset aims to bridge the gap between perceptual tasks (like object detection) and cognitive tasks (like image description and question answering) by providing structured, formalized representations of images in the form of scene graphs.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei (Stanford University, Dresden University of Technology, Yahoo Inc., Snapchat Inc.)
citeAs: Ranjay Krishna et al. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332v1 [cs.CV] 23 Feb 2016
rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. These are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded to Flickr by users. The dataset was collected over 6 months after 15 months of experimentation on data representation. Data collection involved multiple stages: (1) region descriptions with bounding boxes, (2) object extraction from descriptions with bounding boxes, (3) attribute and relationship extraction, (4) region graph construction, (5) scene graph construction by merging region graphs, and (6) question-answer pair collection (both freeform and region-based).
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Crowdsourcing
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from the intersection of YFCC100M (100 million Flickr images) and MS-COCO (328,000 images), resulting in 108,249 real-world photographs. Images range from 72 to 1280 pixels wide with an average width of 500 pixels.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was collected over 6 months following 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For region descriptions: BLEU score thresholds (0.7) were enforced to ensure diversity and prevent repetition of descriptions both within an image and globally across the dataset. For objects: Stanford dependency parser was used to automatically extract nouns as suggestions, which were then verified by workers. Objects from different region descriptions referring to the same entity were merged if their bounding boxes had an overlap over union of 0.8, with human verification. For attributes and relationships: text was lowercased, lemmatized, and excess whitespace was stripped. For canonicalization: all objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases were mapped to WordNet synsets using frequency-based heuristics with hand-crafted rules for common failure cases.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All annotations were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) with over 33,000 unique workers contributing. Region descriptions: Workers drew bounding boxes and wrote descriptions for regions, with each image receiving 50 descriptions collected iteratively. Workers were shown the top 7 most similar existing descriptions (by BLEU score) and required to write dissimilar descriptions. Objects: Workers extracted objects from region descriptions and drew tight bounding boxes satisfying coverage (complete object coverage) and quality (tight fit within 4 pixels). Attributes and relationships: Workers identified attributes of objects and relationships between object pairs from region descriptions. Question-answers: Workers wrote QA pairs following rules to start with one of seven Ws (who, what, where, when, why, how, which), avoid ambiguity, and be answerable from the image. Two types were collected: freeform QAs (8 pairs per image with at least 3 different Ws) and region-based QAs (based on given regions). All annotations went through verification using either majority voting (3 workers, 2/3 agreement required) or rapid judgments for objects.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification was conducted using two strategies: (1) Majority voting where three unique workers voted on each annotation's correctness, requiring at least 2/3 agreement for inclusion. (2) Rapid judgments using an interface inspired by rapid serial visual processing for faster object verification. The dataset achieved a 94.1% retention rate among workers.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image has an average of 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 16 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs. For verification, each annotation received votes from 3 workers in the majority voting process.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers from AMT contributed. Geographic distribution: 93.02% United States, 1.29% Philippines, 1.13% Kenya, 0.94% India, 0.50% Russia, 0.47% Canada, 2.65% others. Age distribution: majority between 25-34 years old, youngest 18 years old, oldest 68 years old. Gender: 54.15% male, 45.85% female.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford NLP tools (Stanford dependency parser) were used to automatically extract noun phrases from region descriptions and QAs as suggestions for workers, achieving 99% recall on a subset of 200 manually annotated region descriptions. WordNet was used for canonicalization of objects, attributes, and relationships to synsets.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains human attributes including gender (man, woman), age-related terms (young, old), and demographic descriptors. Images depict people in various activities and settings.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as shown in the top synsets distribution. There is also a bias towards certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) due to the source image distribution. The images are primarily from Flickr, which may introduce geographic and cultural biases inherent in that platform's user base. 93.02% of crowd workers were from the United States, which may introduce cultural bias in annotations.
rai:dataLimitations: The canonicalization to WordNet synsets is not perfect and contains some ambiguity. Mapping accuracy varies: 86% for objects (98.5% recall), 83.5% for attributes (95.9% recall), and 77.6% for relationships (88.5% recall). The dataset's images come from Flickr and MS-COCO, which may limit diversity compared to a broader sampling of visual content. Relationship prediction experiments showed high intra-class variability, making visual distinction difficult for discriminative models. The dataset focuses on static images and does not capture temporal processes or action sequences.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training and benchmarking models for comprehensive scene understanding tasks including: object detection, attribute prediction, relationship prediction, scene graph generation, dense image captioning, visual question answering, semantic image retrieval, and knowledge base construction. Specific experimental baselines are provided for attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, and question answering. The dataset enables both perceptual tasks (recognition) and cognitive tasks (reasoning about visual content).
